comments.body:
DONE — merged to main. Gerrit 1497 (`63db6ac5a8`) + follow-up 1499 (`52064a9ae7`), both LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1.

DESIGN NOTE the plan surfaced: `transition` already had a valueless `--force` (start-work / plan-review gate bypass) distinct from `--force-close` (close gate). So this was not a pure rename — it is a COLLAPSE of two flags into one `--force[=<reason>]` that bypasses whichever gate the transition would hit, dispatched by target status. No dispatch ambiguity is introduced: on a close the valueless `--force` was already parsed and then discarded (`force` is read only on the start-work path), so no existing invocation changes meaning except by gaining the bypass it asked for by name. A bare `--force` on a close now records `(no reason given)`, matching `claim`.

REJECTION, not silent skip — the load-bearing detail. `_parse_flags` is a hand-rolled loop that SILENTLY SKIPS unknown tokens, so deleting the flag would have made a stale `--force-close="reason"` a silent no-op closing straight through the gate it meant to bypass. The retired spelling is matched explicitly and raises a CommandError naming `--force`. Token comparison is exact, so truncations stay unknown tokens rather than abbreviation-matching onto a live flag. 424f was still `open` at implementation time; this is complementary to its `allow_abbrev=False` work (that targets the argparse-based commands; `transition` does not use argparse), not in conflict with it.

SCOPE decision: the library kwarg `rebar.transition(..., force_close=...)` and the internal `force_close` identifiers keep their names — the ticket renames the CLI flag string only. `transition_compute` gained a `force_reason` keyword so an explicit `--force=<reason>` becomes the start-work audit note, falling back to `--reason` text; `--force --reason=x` is unchanged. The reason propagates through the parent-first cascade.

EXEMPTED from the rename: the three frozen `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/*.jsonl` corpora — recorded LLM-experiment input; rewriting them would corrupt the record. Everything else migrated, including `docs/adr/0043` (it names the live escape hatch, so it was updated in place rather than exempted).

FOLLOW-UP 1499: bug e7a9's secret-screen override landed concurrently with a comment citing `--force-close=` as its flag-shape model. Caught post-merge and fixed so the tree-wide grep is genuinely clean.

VERIFIED ON MAIN: tree-wide grep clean outside CHANGELOG / release-notes / the parser's rejection message and its test; `gen_cli_reference.py --check` passes; new `tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py` (12 tests) passes; full suite green apart from the pre-existing `test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone` failure (reproduced on clean origin/main, unrelated — external jscpd tool). Complexity baseline drained (`_parse_flags` 18 -> 17). CHANGELOG breaking-change entry + `docs/release-notes.md` contract note added. MCP has no force bypass (unchanged).

comments.body:
REOPENED WORK — two defects found post-merge, both fixed in one change.

DEFECT 1 (live on main): `scripts/dependency_audit.py` still emitted the retired flag in the dependency-advisory canary's auto-close argv. It landed via 0767c38ebb (ticket 63e8) which merged AFTER the rename — two concurrent agents crossed, neither could see the other.

RUNTIME IMPACT — verified, not assumed. The parser's explicit rejecting branch fires: CommandError, returncode 1, message 'Error: --force-close was renamed to --force (ticket 24f7) and no longer exists.' `cmd_advisory_alert` does `print(stderr); return rc`, so the canary's auto-close path exits non-zero and the scheduled job goes red. Crucially it is NOT a silent no-op — the rejecting branch this ticket added is what turns it into a loud failure. Fixed to `--force={reason}`, matching the already-migrated `scripts/canary_bridge.py`. No other stale assumption in the surrounding code: `--reason` and `--force=` are independent slots under the new contract and were already passed separately.

DEFECT 2 (why defect 1 survived): the tree-wide acceptance criterion was verified by a one-time manual `git grep` that passed at that moment. Nothing re-checked it, so a file landing minutes later was uncaught. Now committed as a real test.

The exemption set in the AC was VERIFIED rather than trusted, and was wrong in one place: `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` does NOT need exemption — it assembles the literal from parts (`_RETIRED_FORCE_CLOSE = "--force" + "-close"`), so it never carries the string. The earned set is 6 files: the three frozen corpora, CHANGELOG.md, docs/release-notes.md, and this ticket's own test file (its module docstring prose). A second test asserts every exemption is STILL earned, so a stale entry cannot silently widen the blind spot.

Guard derives its file list from `git ls-files` (tracked files), not a directory denylist — the d5ae lesson. Exemptions are exact paths, never directory prefixes, so even a new frozen corpus in the same directory must be consciously weighed.

Also strengthened the call site itself: `test_advisory_alert_close_argv_is_accepted_by_the_real_transition_parser` feeds the emitted argv into the live `_parse_flags`. That is stronger than grep — a future rename fails at the call site whatever it is renamed to. The pre-existing close test asserted only positional slots, which is precisely how the flag escaped the suite.

RED PROVEN BEFORE GREEN for both new tests:
- tree-wide guard: FAILED with exactly one offender, ['scripts/dependency_audit.py'];
- call-site parser test: FAILED with the CommandError above.
Both green after the fix; `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean.

POST-MERGE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED — Gerrit 1504.

The completion verifier's FAIL was right to be suspicious about `scripts/`. A concurrent change (`0767c38ebb`, 63e8 "route dependency advisories by lane") added `scripts/dependency_audit.py` AFTER this ticket's plan review and grep sweep. Its advisory auto-close still emitted the retired close-gate flag, so the argv is now rejected outright and the workflow would have failed the first time it tried to auto-close a cleared advisory — in production, on a path no test exercised.

Why nothing caught it: `tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py` checked the generated argv only POSITIONALLY (`transitions[0][2:5]`) and its `FakeRunner` never executes the command, so no flag was ever validated. Asserting the exact flag string would have moved the same blind spot one inch, so the regression test feeds the generated argv to the REAL `_parse_flags` — any future rename or removal of a flag that builder emits now fails in the suite, whatever it is renamed to. Verified RED against the unfixed script (`CommandError: --force-close was renamed to --force`), GREEN after.

GENERAL LESSON for a flag rename in a busy repo: a grep sweep is only valid as of the sha it ran against. Between plan review and merge, a concurrent change can introduce a NEW emitter of the retired spelling, and a rename that fails loudly (which is what makes the clean break safe) converts that into a runtime break rather than a silent one. Re-run the tree-wide grep against merged main AFTER landing, not only before.

[operator-attested] LOCAL GATE RESULTS (not a repository artifact — recorded here per the AC):
* `ruff check src tests scripts` -> "All checks passed!"
* `ruff format --check src tests` -> "1751 files already formatted"
* `make typecheck` (mypy src/rebar) -> "Success: no issues found in 436 source files"
* `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` -> "active=69 new=0 increased=0 stale=0"
* `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` -> exit 0 (no drift)
* `pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces tests/scripts` -> 10905 passed, 39 skipped, 1 deselected. The single deselection is `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone`, which fails identically on a CLEAN `origin/main` worktree (verified) — it depends on the external `jscpd` tool being installed and is unrelated to this ticket.
* `pytest tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py` -> 12 passed
* `pytest tests/scripts/test_dependency_audit.py` -> 62 passed
* Tree-wide residual check against merged main -> empty (only the CHANGELOG entry, the release-notes note, the parser's rejection branch and its test retain the string, plus the three frozen jsonl corpora).

compiled_state.description:
# Rename `--force-close` to `--force` on `transition` (clean break, no alias)

## Context / Problem
`rebar claim` spells its gate escape hatch `--force[=<reason>]`. `rebar transition` spells the
close-gate escape hatch `--force-close=<reason>` — one concept, two spellings — while ALSO
already accepting a separate valueless `--force` that bypasses the start-work (plan-review)
gate on `open -> in_progress`. So `transition` today has two different force flags with two
different meanings, and neither matches `claim`. Agents and docs get it wrong.

Operator decision 2026-08-07 (recorded as a comment on this ticket): **clean break, no
deprecation alias.** A stale caller must fail loudly with an explicit error, not keep working.
Back-out path if the break proves too disruptive: revert the single rename commit (no alias
exists to fall back on, so callers must update their argv).

## Approach
Collapse `transition`'s two force flags into ONE `--force[=<reason>]` whose meaning is
"bypass whichever gate this transition would hit", dispatched by target status:

- `open -> in_progress`: bypasses the start-work / plan-review gate (today's `--force`
  behaviour, unchanged). The audit note is the `--force=<reason>` value when given, else the
  `--reason` text, else `(no reason given)` — so existing `--force --reason=X` invocations
  keep their exact current behaviour.
- `-> closed`: bypasses the completion-verification / signature gate (today's
  `--force-close=<reason>`). A bare `--force` supplies `(no reason given)`, matching `claim`.

This resolves the collision rather than introducing one: on a close, the valueless `--force`
is currently parsed and then silently discarded (`force` is only read on the start-work path),
so no existing close invocation changes meaning except by gaining the bypass it was already
asking for by name.

Mechanically, `_parse_flags` returns the force reason as `str | None` (`None` = flag absent).
The CLI wrapper derives `force = <not None>` and `force_close = value or "(no reason given)"`
when present, and threads the explicit value to `transition_compute` as a new
`force_reason: str = ""` keyword so the start-work audit note can prefer it over `--reason`.

`transition`'s flag loop is hand-rolled and **silently skips unknown tokens**, so a plain
removal would make `--force-close="reason"` a silent no-op — the worst outcome. The parser
therefore gets an explicit rejecting branch for both `--force-close` and `--force-close=<v>`
that raises a `CommandError` naming `--force`. Because the loop matches tokens exactly (no
prefix/abbreviation matching), no abbreviation hazard is introduced; this is complementary to,
and does not conflict with, ticket 424f's `allow_abbrev=False` work on argparse-based commands.

The library kwarg `rebar.transition(..., force_close=...)` and the internal `force_close`
Python identifiers are **out of scope** and keep their names — this ticket renames the CLI
flag string only.

## Scope
Code:
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — `_parse_flags`, `transition_compute`
  (`force_reason` keyword), `_USAGE`.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/transition.txt` — usage line.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`, `close_precheck.py`, `txn.py`,
  `close_disposition.py`, `_lib_writes.py`, `_config_schema.py`, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`
  — the `--force-close` **flag spelling** in operator-facing error text, docstrings, comments.
- `scripts/canary_bridge.py` — the two argv builders that emit `--force-close=<reason>`.

Docs (every tracked non-frozen file carrying the flag spelling, enumerated from
`git grep -l -- "--force-close"`):
- `README.md`, `rebar.toml`, `docs/cli-reference.md` (regenerated by
  `scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`; CI drift gate), `docs/plan-review-gate.md`,
  `docs/llm-framework.md` (lines ~720, 821, 826, 827), `docs/manifest-signing.md`,
  `docs/bug-creation-contract.md`, `docs/remediation-implementation-plan.md`,
  `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`,
  `docs/adr/0043-operator-attested-completion-evidence.md` (line 19 — the ADR names the LIVE
  escape hatch, so its flag spelling is updated in place rather than exempted),
  `CHANGELOG.md` (breaking-change entry), `docs/release-notes.md` (agent-visible contract
  change).

Explicitly NOT edited — frozen historical corpora whose content is recorded experiment input;
rewriting them would corrupt the record:
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl`
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/exp2_agentic.jsonl`
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/operator_attested_ac_corpus.jsonl`

Tests: the existing tests asserting the old spelling (`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/*`,
`tests/unit/*`, `tests/scripts/test_canary_bridge*.py`), plus a new
`tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py`.

## Testing
- Happy path: `--force="reason"` on a close sets the force-close reason and bypasses the
  completion gate; `--force` on `open -> in_progress` still bypasses the start-work gate.
- Bare `--force` on a close yields the `(no reason given)` reason (parity with `claim`).
- Edge/failure: `--force-close="x"` and bare `--force-close` each raise a `CommandError`
  whose message names `--force`, and are NOT silently skipped by the unknown-token loop.
- Regression: `--force --reason="x"` on `open -> in_progress` still uses `x` as the audit note.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `rebar transition <id> <from> closed --force="<reason>"` bypasses the close gate exactly
      as `--force-close=<reason>` did — verified by a unit test asserting `verify_completion`
      is never invoked on that path.
- [x] A bare `--force` on a close bypasses the gate with the reason `(no reason given)`,
      matching `rebar claim --force` — verified by a `_parse_flags` unit test.
- [x] `--force` on `open -> in_progress` still bypasses the start-work gate — verified by the
      existing start-work gate tests passing unchanged.
- [x] `--force --reason="x"` on `open -> in_progress` still records `x` as the audit note —
      verified by a unit test asserting the note text.
- [x] `--force-close` (with or without a value) exits non-zero with an error message
      containing `--force` — verified by a unit test; it must not be silently skipped.
- [x] The literal flag string `--force-close` survives ONLY in these places, and nowhere
      else in the tracked tree: the three frozen
      `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/*.jsonl` corpora, the `CHANGELOG.md`
      breaking-change entry, the `docs/release-notes.md` contract note, the parser's
      rejection branch in `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`, and its test
      `tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py` — verified by this command exiting 0:
      `test "$(git grep -l -- '--force-close' | grep -vc -e '^docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/' -e '^CHANGELOG.md$' -e '^docs/release-notes.md$' -e '^src/rebar/_commands/transition.py$' -e '^tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py$')" -eq 0`
- [x] `docs/cli-reference.md` is regenerated so the CI drift gate passes — verified by
      `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` exiting 0.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` records the rename under a breaking-change heading — verified by
      `grep -q -- '--force-close' CHANGELOG.md` finding the entry.
- [x] No force flag is exposed over MCP — verified by
      `grep -q 'deliberately NO ``force`` bypass' src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` and no `force`
      field appearing in the MCP transition tool signature.
- [x] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full `pytest` suite pass
      in the worktree. This is a local execution result, not a repository artifact, so it
      is attested in a ticket comment recording the commands and their output.
